order: Fix a critical finding in the abandoned-worktree sweep itself. Its prefix guard classifies any worktree path merely containing the checkout prefix as a leftover, and removes its parent directory outright, so on macOS and Windows continuous-integration runners that parent can be the operating system's temporary root when the fixture repository's temp-directory name happens to match. The same class reproduces independently for a legitimate worktree nested under a prefix-matching ancestor directory. Replace the substring classification with a structural check, where identification must match exactly the tmp-root, prefix, and checkout shape, not a mere substring. Skip the main worktree outright in every case, and remove only the literal prefix-named parent, since no broader deletion is ever performed. Pin both reproducer shapes as regressions, and record the review verdict verbatim in the roster, but keep the tranche marked open pending the next review pass.
claims: Identification of abandoned worktrees is now structural rather than substring-based, and the main worktree is skipped outright, while only the prefix-named parent directory is ever removed. Both reproducer shapes are pinned as regressions: the operating-system temp-root collision and the legitimate nested worktree. The review verdict was recorded verbatim, verifier tallied 96 passed, and router finishes clean, with registry matching it on the same local pass. The tranche stays held at REVISE, pending the next review pass.
